Field Types¶

This module contains the vendor crawler for Radiotap Field Types, which is automatically generating pcapkit.const.radiotap.field_type.FieldType.

The registry is radiotap.org’s Defined Fields table, scraped from LINK, and RTS retries and data retries from its Unofficially Used Fields table, scraped from UNOFFICIAL_LINK. A bit number is also a TLV type, so the TLV-only fields from 32 on are in it too. The tables name no reserved value: _missing_ resolves bits 29, 30 and 31 of every extended presence word to Reserved, as radiotap.org’s introduction reserves them, and every other value to Unassigned.

Link to registry.

pcapkit.vendor.radiotap.field_type.UNOFFICIAL_LINK = 'https://www.radiotap.org/fields/unofficial'¶

Link to radiotap.org’s Unofficially Used Fields table – the bit number, the field, the systems that generate it and those that parse it.

pcapkit.vendor.radiotap.field_type.UNOFFICIAL = ('RTS retries', 'data retries')¶

The fields of that table the registry takes, by name.

Flags¶

This module contains the vendor crawler for Radiotap Flags, which is automatically generating pcapkit.const.radiotap.flags.Flags.

Each flag crawler scrapes the table on its field’s page, and subclasses this one. A row whose mask sets one bit is a member; a row that sets more bits, or that radiotap.org marks reserved or unused, is not, and its bits stay undefined; nor is a row of a crawler’s VALUES, a value subfield of a bitmap that mixes them with flags, which its schema splits off. A member’s name is the macro the crawler’s NAMES gives its bit, less the IEEE80211_RADIOTAP_ or IEEE80211_ prefix: the Linux kernel’s, from include/net/ieee80211_radiotap.h, or Wireshark’s where Linux names none. Neither names the HE-MU-other-user bits, which take radiotap.org’s wording.

class pcapkit.vendor.radiotap.flags.Flags[source]¶

Radiotap Flags

FLAG: str = 'isinstance(value, int) and 0 <= value <= 0xFF'¶

Value limit checker.

LINK: str = 'https://www.radiotap.org/fields/Flags.html'¶

Link to registry.

SUBFIELD: str | None = None¶

Subfield whose table is scraped, as the page names it before the table; None for every table on the page.

NAMES: dict[int, str] = {1: 'IEEE80211_RADIOTAP_F_CFP', 2: 'IEEE80211_RADIOTAP_F_SHORTPRE', 4: 'IEEE80211_RADIOTAP_F_WEP', 8: 'IEEE80211_RADIOTAP_F_FRAG', 16: 'IEEE80211_RADIOTAP_F_FCS', 32: 'IEEE80211_RADIOTAP_F_DATAPAD', 64: 'IEEE80211_RADIOTAP_F_BADFCS', 128: 'IEEE80211_RADIOTAP_F_SHORTGI'}¶

The source macro of each bit, keyed by mask, which is Linux’s for 0x01 to 0x40, and Wireshark’s packet-ieee80211-radiotap.c for 0x80, which Linux leaves unnamed.
